ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows example six-sided polygon outlines that are irregular, and at least one has an inward notch, indicating concave hexagons are allowed rather than only regular or convex hexagons. Reasoning: A simple hexagon has interior angle sum (6 - 2) × 180 = 720 degrees. If all 6 interior angles were right angles, their sum would be 6 × 90 = 540 degrees, which is too small, so 6 right angles are impossible. If 5 interior angles are right angles, they sum to 5 × 90 = 450 degrees, leaving 720 - 450 = 270 degrees for the sixth angle. A 270-degree interior angle is possible in a concave hexagon, matching the kind of concave examples suggested by the image. Therefore, the greatest possible number of interior right angles is 5.
